nodes.title: Reader pass over the staged scripts, batch 1 (Learning): five scripts (c4-ch03-t01, c5-ch02-t03, c5-ch05-t01, c6-ch02-t04, c7-ch05-t01), one fresh Opus reader each, reading every spoken field against its kit and boards; 740k tokens. 886 fields read, 87 faulted (9.8%): 35 were answer marks not grounded in the key; the other 52 (5.9%) were board 17, language 19, giveaway 10, untrue 3, remediation 1, worked example 1, class level 1. Keys: 0 wrong in about 125 cards (every reader solved every card). By field: why 43, prompt 14, point 9, worked 6, joint 6, remediation 3, simpler 2, bridge 2, hook 2. Six of the 10 giveaways are a later card reusing an earlier card's numbers or question.

Every staged script is read in full by an independent reader before a child hears it; no sampling. Order: two new check.mjs rules first (the same question twice in a script; a crossing or outside-angle card posed on angle@1), then batch 1's 52 faults fixed with a second read per rewrite, then the other 25 scripts in batches of 5 (about 3.7M tokens). A mark on a board may be derived only from the card's key. Reason: 5.9% of gated sentences faulted with 3 untrue and 10 giveaways in five scripts, which is about 18 untrue sentences and 60 giveaways across the batch, and the scattered ones are what no predicate finds. Reverse if: after the two predicates a batch faults under 2% with no untrue sentence; then the remaining scripts are sampled (one reader per two scripts).

In production (releases 18 and 19) every bold Latin label on the lesson stage rendered in the system sans (Roboto on Android), and Hindi at weight 400 in the Atkinson stack rendered in the system font, not Mukta. Cause: Chromium picks a family's weight segment before it looks at unicode-range, and the Devanagari face was declared at 400-600 and 700-900 against a Latin 400-700 face, so Latin at 700 and above matched a segment with no Latin glyphs. Found by Studio with CDP's used-font report and canvas widths on the built stage and on taxila.dev in a Pixel 7 emulation; fixed by declaring the same weight ranges for both scripts in every family (Studio bcc7db378), held by tests/r8-font-match-browser.test.mjs (failed before, passes after). The design review of 2026-11-10 judged screens that carried this fault.
